content: <div class="author-description"><p class="p1"><span class="s1">Beverley Blanning MW is a London-based independent wine journalist and the author of Wine Tasting and Biodynamics in Wine. A feature writer and taster for Decanter – and a contributor to other publications around the world – Blanning has judged at numerous wine competitions internationally. She is also a presenter and educator for corporate, consumer and trade events. She was a judge at the Decanter World Wine Awards 2017, but she first judged the competition in 2004.</span></p></div>

title: Obituary: Matthew Jukes (1967-2026)
content: <p>Guy Woodward runs Grand Cru Creative, a creative agency producing content for wine brands, while also contributing occasional articles to various wine titles. He joined Decanter magazine in 2003 and was editor from 2007 to 2012. Thereafter he was editor of Food and Travel magazine, Harrods’ customer titles and Club Oenologique magazine.</p>

title: Decanter World Wine Awards 2026: An uplifting experience
summary: Despite (or perhaps because of ) the headwinds buffeting the wine industry, this year’s Decanter World Wine Awards (DWWA) saw a dramatic uptick in quality. Our DWWA Co-Chair and Decanter Contributing Editor runs his analytical eye over this year’s results, highlights and revelations.
content: <div class="author-description"><p>Andrew Jefford has written for Decanter magazine since 1988.  His monthly magazine column is widely followed, and he also writes occasional features and profiles both for the magazine and for <em><a href="http://www.decanter.com/" target="_blank" rel="noopener" data-saferedirecturl="https://www.google.com/url?q=http://www.decanter.com&amp;source=gmail&amp;ust=1636127504805000&amp;usg=AFQjCNGxcmapJnpHFGMAjETz__znQ1b8Bw">Decanter.com</a></em>. He has won many awards for his work, including eight Louis Roederer Awards and eight Glenfiddich Awards. He was Regional Chair for Regional France and Languedoc-Rossillon at the inaugural Decanter World Wine Awards in 2004, and has judged in every edition of the competition since, becoming a Co-Chair in 2018. After a year as a senior research fellow at Adelaide University between 2009 and 2010, Jefford moved with his family to the Languedoc, close to Pic St-Loup. He also acts as academic advisor to The Wine Scholar Guild.</p><p><strong>Roederer awards</strong> <strong>2016: </strong>International Wine Columnist of the Year</p></div>

title: Pick the unexpected – Central and Eastern European wines to try this summer

content: <div class="author-description"><p>Claire joined <em>Decanter</em> in 2024 with wide-ranging experience in the wine industry including auction, winemaking, communications and journalism. She holds the WSET Diploma in addition to the Italian Wine Scholar Guild and Vinitaly International Academy Wine Ambassador certifications. She enjoys hemisphere hopping: with two vintages under her belt in both Australia’s Yarra Valley and Vittoria in south-eastern Sicily. As Special Projects Editor at <em>Decanter</em>, Claire oversees all commercial content and bespoke projects. A qualified interpreter, she speaks fluent Italian and French and is working on her Spanish, Romanian and German.</p></div>

title: Cin City: Reassessing Cinsault, the unsung hero finally having its moment
summary: Checking-in on the on-going evolution of first-rate Cinsault...
content: <p>Matt Walls is an award-winning freelance wine writer and consultant, contributing regular articles to various print and online titles including Decanter, where he is a contributing editor. He has particular interest in the Rhône Valley; he is chair of the Rhône panel at the Decanter World Wine Awards and is the owner of travel and events company www.rhoneroots.com. </p><p>He writes about all areas of wine, but specialises in the Rhône.</p><p>Matt's latest book, The Smart Traveller's Wine Guide to the Rhône Valley, was published in September 2025.</p>

title: Wine investment: Collectors continue to diversify
content: <div class="author-description"><p>Chris Mercer is a Bristol-based freelance editor and journalist who spent nearly four years as digital editor of <strong>Decanter.com</strong>, having previously been <em>Decanter’s</em> news editor across online and print.</p><p>He has written about, and reported on, the wine and food sectors for more than 10 years for both consumer and trade media.</p><p>Chris first became interested in the wine world while living in Languedoc-Roussillon after completing a journalism Masters in the UK. These days, his love of wine commonly tests his budgeting skills.</p><p>Beyond wine, Chris also has an MSc in food policy and has a particular interest in sustainability issues. He has also been a food judge at the UK’s Great Taste Awards.</p></div>

title: A wine weekend in Northern Virginia: A blend of many worlds
summary: A blend of history, culture and stunning vistas
content: <div class="author-description"><p>Sedale McCall is a wine writer and editor based in Virginia. He's driven by the untold stories of the people and places in the state and along the East Coast. He holds a Level 3 certification from the Wine &amp; Spirits Education Trust.</p></div>
